long_synopsis: Federal agents returned to Minneapolis in force, drawing arrests of protesters and journalists alongside subpoenas against the governor and mayor and withheld federal funding. Nationally, ICE expanded detention infrastructure, deputized local police, and authorized aggressive refugee rescreening, while a deported infant and misclassified naturalized citizens illustrated the human cost. Courts pushed back repeatedly, ruling detentions unlawful and blocking deportations, and the Supreme Court rejected unilateral tariff power, though the administration found a workaround within days. Voting rules bent toward restriction through flawed databases and proposed ICE presence at polls. Surveillance of ICE critics widened alongside media chilling under new FCC guidance. Transparency disputes multiplied over Epstein records and federal archives. The clock held at 7:43 p.m., reflecting a week of matched pressure and resistance rather than calm.
short_synopsis: Minnesota became the week's proving ground as federal enforcement, subpoenas, and funding coercion met court rulings and public resistance in near-perfect balance. Nationally, surveillance, voter restriction, and media pressure expanded even as courts pushed back—leaving the clock unmoved but the standoff unresolved.
